description: Fallback Foundry PoCs: one drop-in test per scenario. Copy the file to foundry/test/Exploit.t.sol, adapt the TODO-marked constants/interfaces to the target's real ABI, run via scripts/run-fork-poc.sh. Passing exploit test = reproduced on fork state. Failing = did NOT reproduce (real signal). Fork-only: no real transactions, no private keys, no --broadcast.

fallbacks.scenario: Authorization on a fixed calldata offset (non-canonical ABI offset bypass)

provenance.note: Modelled from the UniswapV4Router04 exploit (March 2026): swap(bytes,uint256) checked calldataload(164) against caller(), bypassed by shifting the dynamic bytes offset so the router spent a victim's approval.

fallbacks.scenario: EOA-only guard (tx.origin == msg.sender) defeated by an EIP-7702 delegation

provenance.note: Modelled from the POT token exploit on BSC (~$85k; the EOA-only check WAS the flash-loan protection), Gana Payment ($3.1M) and the QNT pool drain. Delegation is simulated as the chain represents it: 0xef0100 || implementation in the account's code.

fallbacks.scenario: Privilege granted to a development account whose private key is published

provenance.note: Modelled from the AlpsCon AI Trade Hub exploit (October 2026, ~152.8k USDC): the reward gate whitelisted the canonical Hardhat account 0xf39Fd6e5..., whose key is published, and the attacker passed every gate with it via EIP-7702.

fallbacks.scenario: Unauthenticated batch executor reaching a privileged call

provenance.note: Modelled from the QNT pool drain (April 2026): a legacy batch(address[],bytes[]) with no access control routed a call through a delegated admin EOA that the pool trusted by address. Also covers the Squid multicall allowance drain.

fallbacks.scenario: Self-attested authorization (the caller is asked whether it is authorised)

provenance.note: Modelled from the FlashLoopAdapter exploit (October 2026, ~$305k): a Safe module authenticated its caller by asking that caller whether the module was enabled, then made an unconstrained call to a caller-supplied router.

fallbacks.scenario: Optional settlement: settle a win, refund a loss after the timeout (free option)

provenance.note: Modelled from the BlockChainCasino finding in the 2026 games set — the only genuinely profitable case among eight weak-randomness games, and one that no entropy rule can see: commit/reveal is bound correctly, but refundBet() returns the full stake after BET_EXPIRATION_BLOCKS while nothing forces settlement.

notPocable.reason: No on-chain exploit: code-quality / hygiene findings with no state or funds at stake.
Bytecode-shape signals, not standalone exploits — use the source-level fallback for the matching scenario.
Analyzer meta-findings (input could not be parsed / report was capped), not vulnerabilities in the target — no harness applies.

An analysis requirement, not a standalone exploit: the finding says the win/payout rule lives in a registered sub-contract and must be READ before any verdict. There is nothing to execute against the reporting contract — the harness would have to be written against the sub-contract once its source is fetched.
